route_definitions.creative_ideation: Cross-domain association, de-novo concept or mechanism invention, creative writing, narrative dialogue, and open-ended brainstorming.
route_definitions.architecture_reasoning: Deductive first-principles system architecture, formal or mathematical proof/derivation, trade-off critique, and multi-system design planning without editing code.
route_definitions.code_implementation: Write, fix, refactor, or test backend, CLI, library, algorithm, configuration, or quantitative/experiment code.
route_definitions.frontend_ui: Implement, refactor, or style user-facing web or desktop UI views, interactive components, charts, layouts, CSS, and animations.
route_definitions.code_audit: Independent read-only review or audit of code, pull requests, diffs, branches, security invariants, or release readiness (even when saving a review report file).
route_definitions.exploration_forensics: Read-only codebase exploration, log/database/metric forensics, and runtime root-cause diagnosis on local evidence without modifying code.
route_definitions.web_research: Gather, verify, and synthesize information from the public web, literature, documentation, or vendor sources into a sourced report.
route_definitions.visual_analysis: Static offline inspection of images, photos, screenshots, or design mockups: OCR, UI layout/mockup diffs, and fine-grained aesthetic, styling, material, or lighting classification.
route_definitions.text_processing: Rule-defined structured text cleaning, translation, format conversion, mechanical extraction, and bounded summarization.
route_definitions.live_loop: Low-latency observe-decide-act loop attached to a live external text, WebSocket, or API stream where per-turn response time affects the outcome.
route_definitions.gui_control: Operate a live desktop, browser, or mobile graphical interface via screenshots, mouse clicks, and keyboard actions, or continuously monitor a live visual screen.

dimension_rubric.anti_inflation_rule: Score ONLY functional work the worker performs, never brief length or Markdown structure. Coordinator headers (`Parent session agent ID`, `工作目录`), role/AGENTS/SKILL docs, communication contracts, and output/receipt paths are boilerplate—ignore them for `primary_level` and `secondary_level`.
dimension_rubric.creativity_vs_architecture: CONTRAST RULE for `creative_ideation` vs `architecture_reasoning`: `creative_ideation` rewards cross-domain association, inventing novel concepts/gameplay/narrative/product mechanisms from thin air, or expressive creative writing (`creativity` primary). `architecture_reasoning` rewards deductive first-principles engineering, distributed/concurrency invariants, mathematical proof, and system migration specs (`coding` primary, `creativity` supporting). When a single worker must BOTH invent a novel cross-domain mechanism AND implement the code, pair `code_implementation` with `secondary_kind: "creative_ideation"`.
dimension_rubric.composite_secondary_kind: CONTRAST RULE for `secondary_kind` & `secondary_level`: Use `secondary_kind: "none", secondary_level: 0` whenever the task belongs to one primary domain (reading files before coding, running pytest/git, or writing unit tests alongside `code_implementation` are NOT separate kinds). Set a distinct `secondary_kind` (`1..3`) ONLY when the worker executes two genuinely distinct domains in one assignment (e.g. `code_implementation` L3 + minor `frontend_ui` L1 tweak; `frontend_ui` L2 + live browser `gui_control` L2; `visual_analysis` L3 + `code_implementation` L2).
dimension_rubric.visual_vs_live_vs_gui: CONTRAST RULE for `visual_analysis`, `live_loop`, and `gui_control`: (1) Static offline image/photo/screenshot inspection is `visual_analysis` (`needs_visual: true`; `1` coarse OCR, `2` UI mockup/layout diff, `3` fine-grained outfit/garment/makeup/material/lighting judgment). (2) Operating a live GUI or watching a dynamic screen is `gui_control` (`needs_visual: true`). (3) Non-GUI live API/WebSocket observe-act loops are `live_loop` (`needs_visual: false`). (4) Writing or fixing software about real-time domains is `code_implementation`, NOT `live_loop`.
dimension_rubric.access_and_local_only: CONTRAST RULE for `access` & `local_only`: `code_audit` is ALWAYS `access: "read-only"` (even when saving a review report file); local repository `code_implementation` and `frontend_ui` are ALWAYS `access: "write"`. `local_only: true` ONLY when depending on un-inlined local files/repos/processes/GUI; `false` when inputs are inlined or from the public web, even if a workspace header or local output path is named.
dimension_rubric.wants_fast: CONTRAST RULE for `wants_fast`: `true` ONLY when affirmatively requesting fast mode, priority tier, urgent/ASAP turnaround, or a pre-reset quota sprint (`pre-reset sprint`, `before quota resets`, `重置前冲刺`) without negation. `false` when negated (`Do NOT use fast mode`, `no rush`), when fast/immediate only describes an in-task step (`click Save immediately`), or when unmentioned.
dimension_rubric.task_count: `"1"` for a single task, including multi-step sequential workflows (`diagnose -> fix -> test -> report`) or homogeneous batch inspection of many items into one output. `"2"`, `"3"`, or `">3"` ONLY when bundling independent deliverables that separate workers could produce in parallel.
dimension_rubric.expected_hours: Measured agent pace: quick check, runbook, single-diff audit, or screenshot check = 0.1-0.25h; standard investigation, bug fix, batch visual audit, or 1-5 file feature with tests = 0.3-0.6h; wide 8+ file refactor or broad web survey = 0.8-2.5h; multi-stage build or sustained multi-hour live loop = 2.5-4h+.
